To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flavor problem in supersymmetry can be solved by the introduction of a U(2) flavor group which breaks to the standard U(1)×U(1)×Z2 symmetry of the MSSM, and that the intergenerational fermion mass hierarchies and the Cabibbo‐Kobayashi‐Maskawa mixing angles are generated from the symmetry breaking parameters.

the small parameters of the supersymmetric flavor problem, the intergenerational mass hierarchies of the quarks and leptons, and the small Cabibbo‐Kobayashi‐Maskawa mixing angles can all be understood without introducing any small dimensionless Yukawas.

the grand unified supersymmetric flavor theory of this thesis provides a natural explanation for the observed fermion mass hierarchies and for the smallness of the Cabibob-Kobayashi Maskawa (CKM) matrix elements Vub, Vtd, and Vts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the properties of the flavor sector of a supersymmetric SU(5) model, in particular, the mass matrices of the quarks and leptons and the mixing matrices which appear in their couplings to the neutralinos and neutral Higgs bosons.
the construction of a grand unified supersymmetric SU( 5) theory which is free from the supersymmetric flavorchanging problem.
the study of the flavor problem in the context of grand unified theories.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have constructed a model with 10 real free parameters which explains the fermion mass ratios and the Cabibbo‐ Kobayashi‐Maskawa mixing angles without introducing small dimension‐ less Yukawa parameters.

we have found a grand unified supersymmetric model which is free from all the flavor changing neutral current problems and also gives a good description of the observed fermion masses and mixing angles.
the flavor structure in the standard model is a reflection of the underlying flavor symmetry of the theory, the flavor symmetry of the grand unified theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the small parameters of the supersymmetric flavor problem, and the quark and leukaemia hierarchies, can be understood as arising from the breaking of a U ( 2 ) flavor sym- metry in an SU ( 5 ) grand unified theory.
the U(2) flavor symmetry is the most natural and economical way to generate the observed quark and leark masses and mixings.

, with a judicious choice of the U(2) symmetry breaking parameters, the small parameters in the fermion mass matrices can be understood as a result of the U( 1 ) symmetry breaking, without having to introduce small dimensionless Yukava couplings.
